react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on two tightly linked biological processes: sulfur amino acid metabolism (specifically the trans-sulfuration pathway connecting cysteine, homocysteine, hypotaurine, and glutathione) and Phase II drug conjugation metabolism (azathioprine ADME and glutathione-dependent detoxification). RaMP ORA identifies the cross-database consensus winner as REACT:R-HSA-1614558 'Degradation of cysteine and homocysteine' (FDR = 1.4×10⁻⁴, fold enrichment 569) and its WikiPathways counterpart WP:WP4504 'Cysteine and methionine catabolism' (FDR = 1.4×10⁻⁴, fold enrichment 554), both driven by the co-occurrence of hypotaurine (KEGG:C00519) and glutathione (KEGG:C00051). The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently recovers 'Methionine and cysteine metabolism' (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism, p = 0.016) via the same two driver metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently nominates KEGG:hsa00430 'Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism' (p = 0.025) as a KEGG-only hit, providing orthogonal validation that hypotaurine is the primary sulfur-containing signal. A secondary axis is the azathioprine/mercaptopurine drug metabolism pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9748787, FDR = 1.4×10⁻⁴), where 6-methylthiopurine (KEGG:C16614) and glutathione form a narrow, high-fold-enrichment pair (fold = 600), consistent with Phase II conjugation of thiopurine drugs. Benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (CHEBI:30614) appears as a lone driver in Phase I functionalization (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR = 0.002), consistent with environmental toxicant exposure and CYP-mediated oxidation. Coumarin (CHEBI:28794) independently hits Phase I/II drug metabolism and xenobiotics metabolism across both RaMP and mummichog. The biological story is one of combined sulfur amino acid stress (elevated hypotaurine and glutathione as markers of trans-sulfuration activation) and Phase II detoxification engagement (glutathione conjugation, azathioprine/thiopurine metabolism), with benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide reflecting an environmental toxicant co-exposure.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP over-representation analysis identified REACT:R-HSA-211859 (Biological oxidations) as the top pathway with FDR=1.24×10⁻⁶ and fold enrichment=132.2, implicating coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine, and glutathione as pathway members. Cross-paradigm mummichog analysis confirmed these metabolites in multiple enriched pathways: glutathione appeared as a shared hit across three MUMM pathways including Histidine metabolism (p=0.0099), Glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism (p=0.0099), and Xenobiotics metabolism (p=0.0099), while hypotaurine and glutathione were co-enriched in MUMM Methionine and cysteine metabolism (p=0.0099). MetaboAnalystR KEGG analysis returned hsa00240 (Pyrimidine metabolism, p=0.0003) as its top hit, consistent with the purine/antipyrine structural theme introduced by 6-methylthiopurine and glutathione. The three complementary methods converge on sulfur amino acid metabolism and Phase II conjugation (glutathione), with coumarin and hypotaurine serving as secondary co-drivers in the biological oxidations hub.
